suggestions: use explicit JOIN syntax instead of comma-separated FROM clause
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
select cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, count(*) cnt1, cd_purchase_estimate, count(*) cnt2, cd_credit_rating, count(*) cnt3 
from customer c
join customer_address ca on c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
join customer_demographics cd on cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
where ca_state in ('IL','TX','ME')
and exists (
    select * 
    from store_sales ss, date_dim d 
    where c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk 
      and ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk 
      and d.d_year = 2002 
      and d.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
)
and not exists (
    select * 
    from web_sales ws, date_dim d 
    where c.c_customer_sk = ws.ws_bill_customer_sk 
      and ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk 
      and d.d_year = 2002 
      and d.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
)
and not exists (
    select * 
    from catalog_sales cs, date_dim d 
    where c.c_customer_sk = cs.cs_ship_customer_sk 
      and cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk 
      and d.d_year = 2002 
      and d.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
)
group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
order by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
limit 100
